name: Bubba Brown
strengths: Brown stems clean and plants hard on out-breaking routes — creates sudden separation at the break (Artavian Hudl / Lowndes).
Brown is sudden after the catch and stays on his feet through first contact to turn short throws into chunk YAC.
Brown works both outside and from the slot with functional vertical gear that pulls away once he’s stacked.
weaknesses: Brown still needs consistency as a pure vertical separator versus length corners who can match his stride early.
comparison: Brown comps to Van Jefferson — 6-1 / ~200 perimeter WR mold; polished route breaks and YAC contact balance after the catch (size-matched to Brown’s 6-1 / 190).
projection: Brown projects as Year-1 package / special-teams WR snaps, Year 2–3 compete for perimeter rotation, with every-down X/Z ceiling as a route separator who creates after the catch.
schemeFit: Brown fits an RPO / rhythm perimeter attack that rewards sharp breaks, stack-and-go juice, and YAC after the catch.
